coupling: The first raster commit grows the compact row-area and row-cover scratch arrays to the pixel stride, without changing the sweep bound. The later wide-accumulator commit derives scanline_width from that compact allocation and uses it for both compact and wide sweeps, while allocating the new wide arrays for ext.width only. On a padded row with more than 127 active edges, the wide sweep accesses a column beyond its allocation. With only the first edit, both sweeps remain bounded by ext.width; with only the second edit, the compact array length keeps scanline_width at ext.width. The unsafe span originates in the first edit and is consumed by the later wide path, so a correct repair must reconcile the shared sweep bound with the storage sizes across both commits. Changing only the edge-count threshold leaves the wide path reachable for denser rows.
